To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality of salt-stressed AVF was evaluated by the fingerprint-activity relationship and that the bioactive markers of AVF were discovered by multivariate statistical analysis and correlation analysis.
we developed a strategy for quality evaluation by establishing a fingerprint-activity model to evaluate the quality and discover the efficacy-associated markers of salt-treated AVFs.
the quality evaluation of salt-treatment Apocyni veneti folium (AVF) was established by fingerprint-activity relationships between chemical fingerprints and the bioactivities.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the quality evaluation of salt-exposed AVF, which could be a useful tool for the development of quality control standards and for the identification of efficacy-associated markers in the quality evaluation of AVF.
the establishment of a fingerprint-activity correlation between chemical fingerprints and bioactivities of AVF samples treated with different levels of salt.
the development of a strategy for quality evaluation based on the fingerprint-activity relationship of salt-treated AVFs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accumulation of flavonoids and polyphenols, as the bioactive markers, in AVF treated with low levels of salt could be the most important factors contributing to the hepatoprotected activity of AVF.

the accumulation of phenolic acids and flavonoids in AVF exposed to salt stress may contribute to the effective scaveng of free radicals, and the hepatoprotection of AVF is closely associated with its polyphenolic constituents, which can provide an important theoretical foundation for the quality evaluation of AVF.
the quality evaluation of AVF should be performed by combining chemical fingerprints, bioactivity, and bioactive markers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

salt treatment of AVF can improve its quality by increasing the accumulation of active components, and the bioactive markers of AVF exposed low levels of salt can be discovered by the fingerprint-activity relationship.
a high dose (1.5 g/kg) of salt-treated AVFs (0, 0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 4%, 6%, 8%, and 10%) was used to establish a fingerprint-activity correlation model for the quality evaluation of AVFs.
the quality evaluation of AVF could be achieved by the fingerprint-activity relationship, and that this method is a promising approach for the quality control of AVF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accumulation of phenolic acids, flavones and flavonols in AVF subjected low levels of salt may be responsible for the hepatoprotectivity.
salt-treated AVF can be used as a hepatoprotective medicine and that the bioactive compounds of AVF exposed low levels of salt can be used as markers for the quality evaluation of AVF.

the chemical fingerprint of AVF exposed with low levels of salt is more similar to the original one and the hepatoprotection effect is more effective, which provides a new way for quality evaluation of AVF.
